reason: Reviewed merged Claude Code Windows session inbox and native standalone lifecycle guidance. Windows inbox tokens, descriptor FILETIME identity and the platform release floor from main remain authoritative. Standalone identity reads use the native helper and normalize its tagged FILETIME against the bare harness descriptor; source development retains its PowerShell reader. Explicit npm migration preserves old owners and remains incomplete through package-manager cleanup. Hook/skill/setup docs retain these distinctions without claiming live native harness or publication proof. Windows cleanup retains its recovery tools when checking installation-file absence raises an access or I/O error; only explicit not-found errors mean absence. Grok uninstall removes only the canonical managed hook file; sibling references remain User-owned and keep native runtime removal incomplete. Reviewed generic and tokenized wake handoff against supplied hook input, the answer acknowledgement contract, skill and notes reference. Both wake forms now tell the agent to use input already supplied in the turn, and invoke receive once only when none was supplied. A wake itself remains non-authoritative and contains no answer or approval. This removes conflicting receive-first wording without changing delivery ownership, trust, setup, native permissions or Account authorization. Existing README, harness setup, readiness and TRUST semantics require no additional change. This wording correction does not claim deterministic automatic-review acceptance; supported read-only verification remains the evidence path after a reviewer questions request provenance.
